top_story: A Gaza deal framework announced on 31 July quickly collided with conditions on the ground: by 1 August, strikes in Gaza had killed seven people and damaged hospital supplies despite Hamas signaling acceptance of the next stage, underscoring how little protection diplomacy still offers civilians already shaped by repeated family loss and displacement. That same day, Iran’s attack on two tankers under US escort in the Strait of Hormuz broadened the confrontation with Washington from military exchange to maritime coercion, pushing energy prices higher and sharpening Gulf fears of a wider war. By 2 August, Trump had delayed new US strikes after Saudi alarm and Iranian threats raised the costs of escalation, suggesting regional pressure is constraining military options more effectively than formal bargaining. The regional picture is one of fragile political openings repeatedly overtaken by force, with civilians and economic lifelines absorbing the immediate consequences.
